contexts.text: A voice crying, or the voice of a cry is a common formula in the Word, and is applied to any noise, disturbance, annoyance, even to what is joyous. Illustrated. Here, it denotes accusation. ().
Hence the bloods cry = guilt.
To cry from the head of the mountains () = to worship the Lord from love. AE 405:12.
Hence many things connected with war are attributed to the Lord, as here to shout, and to cry ().
The cry (of Sodom and Gomorrah) = what is false. AC 2240, Illustrated. AC 2243. AC 2396. AC 2851:7.
As there is falsity from evil, and falsity producing evil, the term cry is here used (), as a kind of general term signifying that which it involves, namely, evil...
They cried to Lot () = falsity from evil raging against good... To cry is predicated of falsity.
Under Angel of God, see these references. AC 2821.
To cry out of heaven = influx. AC 2821. AC 2841.
A cry () = a change.
To give forth a cry, and to cry bitterly () = lament over falsity or truth destroyed.
She cried to the men of the house () = falsities.
I cried with a great voice () = aversion. Explained.
They cried before him, Bend the knee ()... To cry = acknowledgement through faith.
As a cry is an act which corresponds to a living confession or acknowledgement from faith, the ritual of crying was received among the ancients when such a thing was signified. Illustrated.
In the opposite, to cry = no acknowledgement, thus aversion; and it is predicated of falsity. References.
The people cried to Pharaoh for bread () = the need of good for truth. Explained.
To wail, cry, and weep () = to have mercy and to grieve.
If there is no conjoining medium, there is no reception of good... and if man then cries to the Lord there is no hearing, because he cries from evil, thus for himself against all. AC 6852.
(Joseph) cried () = that the effect was near.
(The Sons of Israel) cried () = imploration.
Their cry went up to God () = that they were heard.
I have heard their cry () = the aid of mercy. Cry = imploration. AC 6862.
Therefore they cry () = their great thought... Saying, and speaking = thought, and therefore so does crying; but crying = intense thought, with the full intention of doing.
They cried to Pharaoh () = indignation displayed.
There shall be a great cry in the whole land of Egypt () = interior lamentation.
Wherefore criest thou unto Me? () = 110 need of intercession.
He cried to Jehovah () = supplication to the Lord from grief. To cry = imploration; also interior lamentation; hence also it = supplication from grief.
Moses cried to Jehovah () = interior lamentation, and intercession. Explained.

If in crying he shall cry to Me () = supplication to the Lord for aid. (AC 9217.) The reason intense supplication is expressed by a cry, is that the supplication, even silent, of those who supplicate from the heart, is heard in Heaven as a cry: this happens when men merely think, and still more when they groan, from a sincere heart; this was represented by a cry in the representative Church, and thus it became a ritual among the Jews. The case is the same with those who are teaching; in Heaven they are heard as crying. Not only do the thoughts, but especially do the affections which are of good and truth speak in Heaven; that these speak, and, if they are ardent, that they cry, has been given to know from experience. But affections of evil and falsity are not at all heard in Heaven, even if the man who supplicates from them should cry loudly... but these are heard in Hell, and as cries there too, if they are ardent. SE 4821. SE 4822.
Hearing I will hear their cry () = that they shall be aided.

It is not the voice of the cry victory, and it is not the voice of the cry the thing is lost () = that Heaven acts on one side and Hell on the other; thus falsity against truth and truth against falsity. The voice of a cry, or the voice in shouting = the quality of the interiors of that nation.
Under Day, see this reference.
The men shall cry, and every inhabitant of the land shall howl () = the lack of all truth and good in the Church.
They cried with a great voice () = grief of heart. AE 393, Illustrated.
He cried with a great voice as a lion roareth () = grievous lamentation that the Church is taken away from Him. AE 601.
Under Bear, see these references. AE 711.
Crying with a great voice to him that sat on the cloud () = the supplication of the Angels of Heaven to the Lord. ( = annunciation. AE 910. AE 913. AE 917.)
They cried () = their mourning. AE 1173.
To cry with a great voice () = from Divine zeal. Explained.
Crying () = fear on account of falsities from Hell.
Cry is said of grief and fear on account of falsities from Hell, and consequently on account of devastation thereby. Illustrated.

Cry, however, is said of every affection that breaks forth from the heart; wherefore it is a word of lamentation, of imploration, of supplication from grief, of attestation, of indignation, of confession, nay, of exultation. AE 393:end.
I heard an unwonted cry. TCR 694.
The cry that it alone is orthodox...
Under Wine, see these references. AE 652:7.
Cry () is said of the condemnation of evil; and voice, of that of falsity.
Cry is said of goods.
He cried with a great voice () = a Divine command... Cry is predicated of the good of love.

Crying with a great voice () = adoration from the good of truth, and consequent joy of heart... To cry = interior affection, because a cry is the effect of it; for when a man is in interior affection, and consequently comes into confession, he cries; this is why a cry = every spiritual affection, whether of joy, of grief, or anything else.
The cry of the Chaldeans in the ships () = the destruction of their doctrinal things.
No cry in our quarters () = nowhere any lamentation over the lack of them.
To cry = grief.
